Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Financial Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up and asking questions will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Financial's results for the Q3. With me this morning are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Karen Lopez, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Ellis, Chief Risk Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Credit Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Financial delivered excellent results in the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on expanding our market share, improving our efficiency ratio, strengthening our balance sheet, investing in our people, driving innovation, and meeting our ESG goals.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas of progress. We saw strong stabilization in credit quality, reflected in our provision for credit losses declining significantly year-over-year amid a resilient economy, while maintaining prudent reserves. Deposit growth accelerated with a favorable shift toward low-cost transactional accounts, supporting our funding stability. Loan portfolios expanded solidly across commercial, consumer, and mortgage segments, driven by targeted originations in high-return areas. Our strategic initiatives under UniBank Forward 2027 are advancing rapidly, with notable gains in digital transformation and fee-based revenue streams. Net interest margin expanded through asset yield improvements and funding cost discipline. Finally, revenue diversification efforts have boosted non-interest income to new highs, reducing reliance on traditional interest earnings.

I'll now turn the call over to Karen Lopez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Karen Lopez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning. UniBank Financial reported net income of $1.2 billion for the Q3, or $2.45 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 8% due to higher loan yields and deposit mix optimization. Non-interest income was up 18% driven by wealth management fees, payments growth, and capital markets activity. Our efficiency ratio improved to 58%. We are on track to achieve our financial targets for the year.

Let me dive deeper into some of these dynamics, starting with our net interest margin, which expanded 12 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 3.62%. This builds on two prior quarters of gains, with net interest income rising 6% sequentially to $2.58 billion on average earning assets of $285 billion. On the asset side, yields climbed 18 basis points to 5.45%, supported by the sustained higher rate backdrop from the Fed's 525 basis point hikes, benefiting floating-rate loans and securities roll-downs. Our C&I segment, now 32% of loans, yielded 6.85% with SOFR-linked spreads around 225 basis points, while CRE multifamily added strength at 5.90%. Pricing discipline via our nCino-integrated engine captured extra yield on new business.

Liability costs edged up just 5 basis points to 1.83%, thanks to a stable 28% non-interest-bearing deposit mix and a deposit beta of 45%, below industry averages. We trimmed FHLB advances and brokered CDs by 15%, and digital savings products drew low-cost inflows. The NIM bridge shows asset expansion adding 22 basis points, offset partially by a 7 basis point liability rise and minor drags from day count and securities prepays, landing at 3.62%. Regionally, our Southeast footprint led at 3.75%, while international operations faced some ECB divergence pressures. We've repositioned securities and hedged liabilities proactively, targeting 3.70% or better by year-end with continued loan growth skewed to high-yield areas.

Shifting to deposit growth and mix, our total deposits hit $285 billion, up 9% year-over-year and 3% sequentially, beating FDIC industry averages. Core deposits excluding brokered grew 11%, with $12 billion in net new money from payrolls and campaigns. Transactional accounts rose to 48% of the mix at $137 billion, growing 14% on treasury management wins and real-time payment integrations like RTP and FedNow—we added 1,200 business clients. Savings at 37% or $105 billion saw betas at 285 basis points but stabilized with tiered products up to 4.75% APY recapturing outflows. Time deposits dipped 8% to $43 billion as maturities rolled off, with costs easing to 4.2%.

Our beta of 42% outperforms peers, with Sunbelt markets surging 15% on migration trends. Strategies include UniBank 360 app upgrades like AI round-ups and FlexCD ladders, driving 25% mobile user growth, alongside cross-sell programs and embedded finance pilots. We expect 7-9% full-year growth, with transactional share to 50%, positioning us for loan funding without margin strain.

On loan growth, average loans reached $285 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year—above the 5.1% peer average per FDIC data. Organic growth hit 8.4% excluding CRE repositioning, with net charge-offs at 28 basis points. Commercial loans, 50% of the book, grew 9.8% to $142 billion: C&I up 12.1% to $95 billion on capex in manufacturing and tech, plus equipment finance tied to reshoring; CRE steady at 4.2% with industrial up 15% on e-commerce demand, keeping office exposure low at 8%. Southeast drove 11.2% gains, aided by AI origination cutting times to 4 days.

Consumer loans expanded 6.5% to $68 billion, led by auto at 9.2% with $4.2 billion originations at 92% LTVs via dealer channels, personal loans via alternative data scoring holding delinquencies at 1.2%, and cards on rewards spend. Mortgages grew 2.1% to $75 billion on purchase volume in migration markets like Florida, with digital closings at 78%. We guide 7-8% full-year growth, backed by tech investments and diversification.

Turning to provision for credit losses, we recorded $450 million, down 25% year-over-year from $600 million and flat sequentially. This tracks credit stabilization in a soft-landing economy, with allowance for loan losses at $12.5 billion or 1.25% of loans, up slightly from 1.22%. Net charge-offs were $380 million or 38 annualized basis points, in our 35-45 bps range. Under CECL, drivers include macro forecasts like Fed dot plot GDP at 1.8% for 2025, unemployment to 4.3%, and Moody's scenarios yielding a $100 million consumer tailwind as PDs eased 15-20 basis points.

Our $1 trillion book—40% commercial, 30% consumer, 20% mortgages, 10% cards—shows past-dues at 1.15% and NPLs at 0.85%. Consumer released $50 million on falling delinquencies to 1.8% via telematics; cards provisioned $120 million flat with 28% utilization; mortgages built $80 million modestly; commercial pressured at $250 million, especially CRE office with vacancy rises, offset by C&I releases. Regions vary, with U.S. Southeast strong and Europe adding modest stress.

Methodology pools by risk traits, projecting ECLs with logistic PD models incorporating 200+ variables, ML ensembles improving accuracy 12%, LGD from workout data, EAD curves, and 1,000+ Monte Carlo runs on AWS-Snowflake. We've added climate proxies and derisked $10 billion CRE, guiding Q4 at $400-500 million.

Revenue diversification has been transformative, with non-interest income at $2.8 billion, up 18% and 42% of total revenue. Wealth management grew 22% to $1.2 billion on $450 billion AUM and robo-tools; payments up 32% to $850 million via PayAPI processing $1.2 trillion; capital markets 14% to $550 million on IPOs and trading; emerging ESG/digital added $250 million with green loans and ETF custody. Mix shifted from 68% NII in 2022 to 58% now, cutting volatility and lifting ROTE to 14.2%. We target 45-50% fee mix by 2026 with tech investments.

Finally, on key strategic initiatives under UniBank Forward 2027, digital transformation advanced with $450 million invested, 85% cloud migration slashing settlement times 92%, 18 million app users, AI personalization boosting cross-sell 18%, and fraud down 35%. Fee businesses scaled AUM 32%, payments 22%; sustainable finance hit $35 billion mobilized; efficiency held expenses flat, closing branches for 200 bps gains. These deliver 8-10% EPS CAGR.

Tom Ellis:
Thank you, Karen. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring commercial real estate pressures and interest rate volatility. We are taking proactive steps like syndication and early warning systems to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

Maria Gonzalez:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing loans at 0.85% and past-due 30+ days at 1.15%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio through conservative underwriting and vintage analysis, remaining confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for queuing up questions via telephone: press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Mike Harlan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Harlan:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the drivers and methodology behind your provision for credit losses, particularly the CRE component?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. As Karen detailed, the $450 million provision reflects macro stabilization and portfolio performance, with CRE driving the uptick due to office vacancies—we've addressed this by syndicating exposure and enhancing PD models. Our CECL framework with ML overlays ensures prudent coverage at 1.25%, and we're positioned for potential releases ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What is your strategy for deposit growth and mix heading into potential rate cuts?

Karen Lopez:
Great question, Lisa. We're targeting 7-9% growth with transactional accounts to 50% mix via digital innovations like UniBank 360 and relationship cross-sell. Our low beta of 42% and Sunbelt momentum give us an edge, allowing us to fund loans without NIM erosion even if cuts materialize.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
How are you addressing risks in commercial real estate lending?

Tom Ellis:
Thanks, David. We're derisking selectively—syndicating $10 billion in office loans YTD, limiting exposure, and using AI early warnings that flag 15% more risks. Regional granularity and stress testing keep our profile robust, aligned with Fed scenarios.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Keefe, Bruyette & Woods. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
Can you update us on loan growth by segment and any shifts in drivers?

Maria Gonzalez:
Absolutely, Sarah. We hit 7.2% overall growth, with commercial at 9.8% on C&I capex and industrial CRE, consumer at 6.5% led by auto, and mortgages at 2.1% on purchases. Underwriting stays tight—FICOs at 745 average—and tech like Pinnacle Originate accelerates while preserving quality.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Alex Rivera for any closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Financial. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
